name: Logistics & Supply Chain
eyebrow: Automation for couriers, freight forwarders, 3PL warehouses and fleet operators
headline: Catch exceptions early. Deliver, bill and settle faster.
summary: MoreSpace designs and builds automations that connect bookings, documents, tracking, deliveries, billing and settlements across your TMS, WMS, GPS and accounts. Your systems stay the record, people approve every rate, filing, claim and payment, and each workflow is measured against KPIs agreed with your team.
shareText: How MoreSpace automates logistics: WhatsApp bookings, proactive delay alerts, NDR resolution, customs checklists, e-way bill and document expiry alerts, POD-to-invoice and COD reconciliation.
audience: Founders and managing directors of courier, transport and 3PL companies
Pricing, documentation and key account managers at freight forwarders

challenges.title: Tracking data that nobody is watching
challenges.description: Milestones sit in the TMS, carrier portals, GPS dashboards and WMS screens, but no one compares them with what was promised. Delays, stuck consignments and missed cut-offs surface when the customer calls, and the same lanes, hubs and carriers keep failing without evidence to fix them.

challenges.title: Failed deliveries that become returns
challenges.description: Consignees are unreachable, addresses lack landmarks and some attempts are recorded without a real visit. Re-attempt instructions arrive after the rider has left, and shipments that could have been delivered come back as return-to-origin costs for the merchant and the network.

challenges.title: Paper that slows billing and clearance
challenges.description: Physical PODs, LR copies, invoices and customs documents travel by hand. Billing waits for PODs, clearance waits for a missing certificate or a corrected invoice, and detention and demurrage build up while teams chase paperwork.

challenges.title: Documents and permits that expire unnoticed
challenges.description: Driver licenses, permits, fitness certificates, PUC certificates, insurance and e-way bills all have expiry dates. When they live in folders and WhatsApp photos, a lapse is found at a checkpoint, in an accident claim or during a client audit.

challenges.title: Cash and charges that do not reconcile
challenges.description: COD collections pass through riders, branches, banks and UPI. Trip advances, fuel and tolls are claimed on paper. Storage and handling charges are assembled at month-end. Reconciliation runs on spreadsheets and differences are found weeks later.

challenges.title: Compliance built into every movement
challenges.description: GST e-way bill rules, Motor Vehicles Act documents, customs filing timelines, carrier registration, messaging consent and the DPDP Act all shape how bookings, trips, updates and consignee data may be automated. A shortcut in one workflow can create risk in another.

flagship.title: Shipment exception desk: proactive delay, NDR and SLA alerts
flagship.summary: One connected workflow that watches every shipment against what was promised, from pickup to proof of delivery. Milestones from your TMS, carrier feeds, GPS and WMS are compared with SLAs, exceptions get an owner and a deadline, consignees and shippers hear about delays and failed attempts before they call, and their choices flow back into the next dispatch plan.

steps.title: Unify every milestone
steps.description: Booking, pickup, hub, line-haul, customs, out-for-delivery and delivery events from the TMS, courier and carrier APIs, GPS platforms and the WMS flow into one shipment timeline with the promised date and contract SLA.

steps.title: Detect exceptions early
steps.description: Rules tuned per lane, service and customer flag missed pickups, no-movement, stuck-at-hub, ETA slippage, vessel rollovers, missed warehouse cut-offs and failed delivery attempts, with reason codes from the source system.

steps.title: Give each exception an owner
steps.description: Each exception lands in the control-tower queue with an owner, a deadline and a suggested next step. Owners are alerted in Slack, and cases still open as the SLA limit approaches escalate to the branch or operations head.

steps.title: Tell the customer first
steps.description: Consignees and shippers who opted in get an approved WhatsApp template with the revised ETA or the failed-delivery reason and choices: re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact or pickup point. Others get the same choices by DLT-registered SMS.

steps.title: Act on the reply
steps.description: Button replies are written back to the TMS before the next dispatch plan. An AI model classifies free-text replies, and unclear or disputed ones go to an agent with the shipment history attached.

steps.title: Close the loop and learn
steps.description: PODs, resolution codes and SLA outcomes feed a dashboard by lane, hub, carrier, merchant and client, so the weekly review fixes recurring causes instead of answering individual complaints.

flagship.humanCheckpoint: Control-tower executives own every exception and approve messages to key accounts, NDR agents handle unclear or disputed replies, hub supervisors review questionable attempts, and merchants approve returns and out-of-rule address changes. No automated message promises compensation or an unconfirmed delivery time.
outcomes: Customers hear about delays and failed attempts from you before they call
Fewer deliverable shipments turned into returns to origin
Every exception has a named owner, a deadline and a recorded resolution
Reason-coded data that shows which lanes, hubs and carriers need fixing

stages.title: Enquiry & quote
stages.description: A shipper, importer or e-commerce brand asks for rates for a lane, a container, a monthly parcel volume or warehouse space. The same request often goes to several providers, so a complete quote on current rates, sent quickly, decides who gets the booking.
touchpoints: Spot and contract rate requests by email

stages.title: Booking & pickup request
stages.description: The shipper books a pickup, a container or a truck. Details captured here decide what follows: address, ready time, weight and dimensions, declared value, payment mode and whether an e-way bill or special handling is needed.
touchpoints: Orders pushed from seller platforms and APIs
stages.owner: Booking desk or customer service lead

stages.title: Vehicle & driver assignment
stages.description: Before a vehicle is placed or a rider is sent out, operations match the load to a vehicle, confirm the driver and check licenses, permits, fitness, insurance, PUC and maintenance. A lapse found here means rescheduling; found at a checkpoint or after an accident, it means a detained vehicle or a disputed claim.

stages.title: Pickup, receipt & origin handling
stages.description: Goods are picked up from the shipper or arrive at the hub or warehouse. They are scanned, weighed and received against the booking or ASN, and the LR, invoice and e-way bill travel with them. Discrepancies recorded here protect everyone later.
touchpoints: First-mile pickup scan and weight capture
LR or goods receipt and e-way bill

stages.title: In transit, at hubs & at customs
stages.description: Line haul, hub transfers, ocean and air legs and customs clearance. Most delays happen here, documents and e-way bills must stay valid, and customers ask where their shipment is.
touchpoints: GPS, hub scans and carrier milestones
E-way bill validity and Part B updates
Customs filing, queries and out of charge

stages.title: Delivery, NDR & proof of delivery
stages.description: Out for delivery, delivered or failed. Failed attempts need a quick, honest reason and a consignee choice, and every delivery needs proof that billing and claims can rely on.

stages.title: Billing, settlement & review
stages.description: Freight and warehouse invoices go out, COD is remitted to merchants, drivers' trip expenses are settled and clients review stock, SLAs and charges. Accuracy here decides cash flow and whether the client renews.
touchpoints: Client stock statements and SLA reviews
stages.owner: Finance controller with the key account manager

segments.name: Courier & last-mile delivery
segments.headline: More first-attempt deliveries, fewer returns, faster COD.
segments.summary: For express couriers, e-commerce last-mile networks, hyperlocal fleets and regional delivery partners. We connect merchant bookings, rider onboarding, tracking, failed-delivery handling and COD settlement, so branches act on exceptions the same day and merchants and consignees hear from you before they call.
challenges: Failed deliveries are recorded with vague or questionable reason codes and turn into return-to-origin costs for merchants and the network.
Merchants and consignees call branches for pickup and delivery status because updates are late or generic.
COD cash passes through riders, branches, banks and UPI before remittance, and reconciliation runs on spreadsheets.
High rider turnover means constant onboarding, with licenses, vehicle papers and verification tracked by hand.
Pickups booked after cut-off or with wrong weights lead to missed pickups and billing disputes.

uses.title: Pickup booking on WhatsApp and the portal
uses.description: Merchants book pickups through a WhatsApp Flow, the portal or an API, with serviceability, restricted-item and weight checks before a slot is confirmed.

uses.title: NDR resolution with consignee choices
uses.description: Consignees confirm or correct the failure reason and choose a re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact or pickup point, written back before the next dispatch plan.

uses.title: Proactive delay updates
uses.description: Shipments that stall at a hub or miss their promised date get an owner and a consignee update before the first complaint.

uses.title: COD reconciliation and merchant remittances
uses.description: Rider collections, branch deposits and UPI settlements are matched to AWBs daily, and remittance files with statements are prepared for finance to release.

uses.title: Rider onboarding and document expiry tracking
uses.description: License, registration, insurance and PUC are collected with consent, verified and tracked to expiry, so riders with lapsed documents are not assigned.

uses.title: Where-is-my-parcel assistant
uses.description: Consignees and merchants get answers from live tracking on WhatsApp, with handover to an agent for claims, damage and refunds.

kpis: Pickups completed in the booked slot
systems: Courier TMS or last-mile platform such as Shipsy or LogiNext
Rider app with GPS and call logs
Seller platforms and aggregators such as Shopify or Shiprocket
Payment gateway and UPI settlement reports

segments.name: Freight forwarding & customs
segments.headline: Quotes out sooner. Documents right before the broker files.
segments.summary: For freight forwarders, NVOCCs, customs brokers and multimodal operators handling ocean, air and cross-border road cargo. We automate rate requests, document checklists and clearance milestones around your forwarding software and your licensed customs broker, so pricing and documentation teams spend their time on judgment instead of copying data.
challenges: Rate requests arrive in every format, and buy rates, surcharges and validity dates live in scattered sheets and emails.
Clearance stalls on missing or mismatched documents that nobody spotted until filing.
Importers and exporters call repeatedly for milestone updates while port and CFS free time runs down.
Vessel rollovers, blank sailings and ETA changes reach customers late, sometimes from the shipping line before the forwarder.

uses.title: RFQ-to-quote with rate cards
uses.description: Requests are structured, priced from current buy rates and surcharges with validity checks, and approved by the pricing lead before they are sent.

uses.title: Document checklists by commodity and destination
uses.description: Each shipment gets a checklist from HS code, Incoterm, origin and destination, with reminders to the shipper tied to the arrival date and Bill of Entry timeline.

uses.title: Cross-document mismatch checks
uses.description: AI compares the invoice, packing list and bill of lading for value, quantity, weight, consignee and HS code differences before the broker files.

uses.title: Clearance milestone updates
uses.description: Filing, query, assessment, duty payment and out-of-charge statuses are posted to the shipment record and shared with the customer.

uses.title: Rollover, ETA and free-time alerts
uses.description: Schedule changes from shipping lines and airlines, and free time running out at the port or CFS, reach the owner and the customer early.

uses.title: Shipment status assistant
uses.description: Customers ask on WhatsApp or web chat about bookings, containers and clearance, and get answers from the forwarding system, with handover to the documentation team.

kpis: Clearance time from filing to out of charge
systems: Freight forwarding software such as CargoWise or Magaya
Shipping line and airline booking portals

segments.name: Warehousing & 3PL
segments.headline: Clients see their stock without asking. Billing closes on time.
segments.summary: For contract logistics providers, e-commerce fulfillment centers, and cold-chain and bonded warehouses serving several clients. We connect ASNs, receiving, order cut-offs, client reporting and activity-based billing around your WMS, so clients get timely, accurate information and finance bills everything the contract allows.
challenges: Every client sends ASNs, orders and report requests in its own format, and the team re-keys or reformats them.
Short, excess and damaged receipts are noted on paper and reach clients too late to claim against suppliers or transporters.
Orders that will miss the carrier cut-off are noticed only after the truck has left.
Storage, handling and value-added charges are assembled at month-end from several reports, and some are never billed.

uses.title: ASN-to-GRN tracking
uses.description: ASNs from EDI, email or the portal are validated and matched to receipts, and GRN summaries with photo evidence go out as soon as receiving closes.

uses.title: Order cut-off and SLA watch
uses.description: Orders still unpicked or unpacked as the carrier cut-off approaches are flagged to the shift lead, and clients hear about breaches with a reason.

uses.title: Scheduled client stock statements
uses.description: Stock, ageing, batch and near-expiry statements go to each client on schedule, in the format they need, from one warehouse data model.

uses.title: Activity-based billing
uses.description: Storage and handling charges are calculated from WMS activity and contract rate cards, with exceptions reviewed before finance approves the invoice.

uses.title: Client query assistant
uses.description: Clients ask about receipts, stock and order status on WhatsApp or the portal and get answers from the WMS, with handover to the account manager.

kpis: Orders dispatched before the carrier cut-off
systems: WMS such as Unicommerce, Increff, Vinculum or SAP EWM

segments.name: Fleet & road transport
segments.headline: Road-ready vehicles, faster billing, cleaner trip settlements.
segments.summary: For full-truckload and part-truckload transporters, fleet owners, contract fleets and operators who also run attached market vehicles. We automate document and maintenance tracking, e-way bill validity, delay alerts, POD-to-invoice and trip settlements around your TMS, GPS and accounts, with your fleet manager and finance team approving every decision.
challenges: Licenses, permits, fitness certificates, PUC and insurance expire on different dates across owned and attached vehicles.
Physical PODs arrive weeks after delivery, so billing waits and detention charges go unclaimed.
Trip advances and expense claims are settled by hand with little link to fuel card, FASTag or GPS data.
E-way bills expire while trucks wait at hubs or consignee gates, and the team finds out at a checkpoint.
Shippers hear about breakdowns and delays when they call, not from the transporter.

uses.title: Driver and vehicle document register
uses.description: Documents are collected, checked against VAHAN and SARATHI records and tracked to expiry, and assignment is blocked when something lapses.

uses.title: Preventive maintenance from odometer data
uses.description: GPS odometer readings drive service, tire and inspection reminders, and drivers report defects with photos and voice notes on WhatsApp.

uses.title: E-way bill validity watch
uses.description: Validity is compared with the GPS-based ETA, with alerts in the extension window and Part B reminders when goods change vehicles.

uses.title: Digital POD to invoice
uses.description: PODs captured in the driver app or on WhatsApp become draft invoices, with detention charges calculated from recorded arrival and unloading times.

uses.title: Trip expense and fuel settlement
uses.description: Receipts are read from photos and checked against fuel card, FASTag and GPS data before the fleet manager approves the settlement.

uses.title: Delay alerts to shippers
uses.description: Breakdowns, no-movement and ETA slippage create an exception with an owner and a shipper update before the promised delivery time passes.

kpis: Vehicles or drivers with a lapsed document
systems: GPS or telematics platform such as Fleetx, LocoNav or WheelsEye
VAHAN and SARATHI records via ULIP or an authorized provider
E-way bill system via GSP or ERP

automations.title: Freight RFQ-to-quote with rate cards and margin approval
automations.summary: Read spot and contract rate requests from email, WhatsApp and tender portals, structure them, price each lane from your own buy rates, surcharges and validity dates, and give the pricing lead a draft quote to approve before it reaches the shipper.
automations.problem: Rate requests arrive as emails with attachments, WhatsApp messages and portal tenders, each in a different format. Pricing staff search carrier contracts, co-loader offers and surcharge notices by hand, rates expire before quotes go out, and margins vary with whoever quoted. Shippers who send the same request to several forwarders tend to book with the first complete, valid quote.
automations.trigger: A rate request lands in the pricing mailbox, arrives in a WhatsApp chat the shipper started, comes through the website form, or is exported from a customer tender portal.
steps: Collect requests from the pricing mailbox, WhatsApp, web forms and tender exports into one queue, matched to existing customer accounts in the CRM.

Use an AI model to extract origin and destination, Incoterm, commodity and HS code, container type or weight and volume, cargo-ready date and special handling, and list missing details as questions for the sales rep.

Look up current buy rates from carrier contracts, co-loader offers and the rate sheet, add surcharges such as BAF, THC and documentation fees, and exclude rates whose validity ends before the cargo-ready date.
Apply the agreed margin rules by customer tier and lane, and build a draft quote with routing options, transit times, free time, validity and exclusions.
Send the draft to the pricing lead in a review screen; quotes below the margin floor go to the branch or commercial head.
Send the approved quote as a PDF from the rep's address, schedule follow-ups in the CRM and record won or lost reasons by lane.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The pricing lead approves every buy rate, margin and routing before a quote is sent, and the commercial head approves anything below the margin floor or with non-standard credit terms. The automation never commits space, rates or sailings on its own.
systems: Freight forwarding software such as CargoWise or Magaya
Carrier contracts and co-loader rate sheets
CRM such as Zoho CRM or HubSpot
automations.data: Uses business contact details and shipment particulars the shipper sent. Buy rates and margins are commercially sensitive and visible only to pricing and sales leadership; reps see sell rates. Raw emails and attachments are kept for an agreed troubleshooting period and then deleted, while approved quotes follow the client's record retention policy.
kpis: Margin variance from the agreed matrix
outputs: Unified rate request queue with extraction rules
Rate and surcharge lookup with validity checks
Quote PDF template and follow-up schedule
Win-loss dashboard by lane and customer

automations.title: Booking and pickup scheduling on WhatsApp and the portal
automations.summary: Let merchants book pickups through a WhatsApp Flow, the portal or an API, check serviceability, restricted items and weight before accepting, assign a pickup slot by branch cut-off, and confirm with the AWB, labels and a reminder.
automations.problem: Small merchants book pickups by calling or messaging a branch, often after the daily cut-off, with incomplete addresses, wrong weights or unserviceable pin codes. Riders arrive to find parcels unpacked or not ready, missed pickups go unexplained to the merchant, and weight disputes surface later at billing.
automations.trigger: A merchant completes the WhatsApp booking Flow, creates a shipment in the portal, or pushes orders through the API or a connected seller platform.
steps: Capture pickup address, ready time, number of packages, declared weight and dimensions, payment mode and declared value through a WhatsApp Flow, portal form or API.
Check pin code serviceability, COD limits, prohibited and restricted items, and whether the declared value needs an e-way bill number before pickup.
Create the shipment and AWB in the courier TMS, assign a pickup slot by branch cut-off and rider route, and send the merchant a confirmation with labels.
Remind the merchant before the slot, and alert the branch when a rider is running late or a pickup is at risk of being missed.
Record pickup scans and measured weight; when it differs from the declared weight beyond the agreed tolerance, attach dimensioner photos and notify the merchant.
Send failed pickups to the branch supervisor with the reason, and offer the merchant the next available slot.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Branch supervisors approve exceptions such as pickups after cut-off, restricted items and high-value or bulk pickups. Weight disputes are decided by the billing team using the photos and dimension records, never by the automation.
systems: Seller platforms such as Shopify or Unicommerce
automations.data: Uses merchant business details, pickup addresses and the consignee details needed for the label. WhatsApp messages go only to merchants who opted in. Weight photos are kept for the dispute window in the merchant contract and then deleted. Branch staff see only their own branch's bookings.
kpis: Pickups completed in the booked slot
outputs: WhatsApp booking Flow and portal booking form
Pickup slot assignment and reminder templates

automations.title: Driver and rider onboarding with document expiry alerts
automations.summary: Collect and verify driver and rider documents at onboarding, track every expiry date for licenses, registration, insurance, PUC, fitness and permits, and stop a vehicle or driver with a lapsed document from being assigned.
automations.problem: Licenses, registration certificates, insurance, PUC certificates, fitness certificates and permits expire on different dates and sit in folders, WhatsApp photos and spreadsheets. Lapses come to light at a checkpoint, during an accident claim or in a client audit. Courier networks onboarding many riders, including riders on their own two-wheelers, face the same problem at higher volume.
automations.trigger: A new driver or rider applies, a vehicle is added to the fleet, a document enters its reminder window before expiry, or a trip assignment is about to be confirmed.
steps: Collect documents through a WhatsApp Flow or onboarding form after a clear notice and consent, accepting DigiLocker-issued copies the applicant chooses to share.
Use OCR and an AI model to read names, numbers and expiry dates, and check license and registration details against VAHAN and SARATHI records through ULIP or an authorized verification provider.
Store each document with its expiry date in a compliance register per driver and vehicle, and flag mismatches such as a license class that does not cover the vehicle type.
Remind the driver, the vehicle owner and the fleet manager at agreed intervals before each expiry, and collect the renewed document in the same chat.
Check validity at trip assignment and hold confirmation of any driver or vehicle with a lapsed document until the fleet manager clears it.
Report upcoming expiries, lapses and renewals by branch, vendor and vehicle type.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The fleet or HR manager approves every onboarding after reviewing flagged mismatches, and decides any exception to the assignment hold. Background verification results are reviewed by a person; the AI model only reads and compares documents.
systems: VAHAN and SARATHI records via ULIP or an authorized provider
automations.data: Driver and rider documents are personal data. We collect only what the role and the law require, with a clear notice and consent, keep documents encrypted with access limited to HR and fleet managers, and do not store full Aadhaar numbers. Documents of drivers and riders who leave are deleted after the agreed retention period.
kpis: Vehicles or drivers with a lapsed document
Onboarding time from application to approval
outputs: Onboarding Flow and document checklist by role
Compliance register for drivers, riders and vehicles

automations.title: Preventive maintenance and tire reminders from odometer data
automations.summary: Use GPS odometer readings and service history to schedule preventive maintenance, tire rotation and inspections for each vehicle, warn dispatch before a due vehicle is assigned, and track work orders to closure.
automations.problem: Service intervals are tracked in a register or in the mechanic's memory. Vehicles skip services during peak season, breakdowns strand loads mid-route, and tires and batteries are replaced without history. Dispatch cannot see which vehicles need workshop time when planning the week.
automations.trigger: A vehicle's GPS odometer reading crosses a service threshold, a date-based interval is reached, a driver reports a defect, or a vehicle is selected for a trip.
steps: Pull daily odometer and engine-hour readings from the GPS or telematics platform and reconcile them with trip and fuel records.
Calculate the next service, tire rotation, battery check and inspection due points for each vehicle from the maintenance plan and service history.
Alert the maintenance supervisor and dispatcher as a vehicle approaches a due point, and suggest a workshop slot that fits the trip plan.
Let drivers report defects with photos and voice notes on WhatsApp; an AI model turns them into structured defect reports for the supervisor.
Create and track work orders with parts, cost and downtime, and mark the vehicle unavailable in the TMS until the supervisor closes the job.
Report planned and unplanned maintenance, downtime and cost per kilometer by vehicle and route.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The maintenance supervisor decides whether a defect makes a vehicle unfit to run, approves any deferral of a due service and signs off completed work orders. Brake, steering, tire and other safety-related defects reported by drivers always go to a person.
systems: GPS or telematics platform such as Fleetx, LocoNav or WheelsEye
automations.data: Vehicle telemetry is linked to drivers, so location data is used only for maintenance and trip purposes, with access limited to fleet and maintenance staff. Driver defect reports are stored with the work order. Retention follows the client's policy for vehicle and maintenance records.
outputs: Due-point alerts for supervisors and dispatch
WhatsApp defect reporting and work order tracker

automations.title: Inbound ASN-to-GRN tracking with discrepancy alerts
automations.summary: Match each client's advance shipping notice with the vehicle at the dock and the goods received, flag short, excess and damaged lines with photos, and send the client a GRN summary as soon as receiving closes.
automations.problem: Clients send ASNs as emails, spreadsheets or EDI files, and trucks arrive without appointments. Receiving teams count against printed lists, discrepancies are noted on paper, and clients learn about shortages or damage days later when stock does not show as available. Claims against suppliers and transporters then lack timely evidence.
automations.trigger: A client ASN arrives by EDI, API, email or the client portal, a vehicle reports at the gate, or receiving is closed for an inbound in the WMS.
steps: Read ASNs from EDI, API, email attachments or the portal, validate SKU codes, quantities, batch and expiry fields against the client's item master, and create the expected receipt in the WMS.
Offer dock appointment slots to the client or transporter, and alert the dock supervisor when a vehicle arrives without an ASN or appointment.
During receiving, compare scanned quantities, batches and expiry dates with the ASN, and capture photos of damaged cartons and broken seals in the handheld app.
When receiving closes, generate a GRN summary with short, excess and damaged lines and photo links, and send it to the client's nominated contacts.
Open a discrepancy case for each variance with an owner and deadline, and track it until the client confirms acceptance, a return or a claim.
Report dock-to-stock time and discrepancy rates by client, supplier and transporter for the weekly review.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The receiving supervisor confirms every discrepancy before the GRN summary is released, and the client's nominated contact decides whether to accept, return or claim against short or damaged goods. Quarantine and release of damaged or expired stock stay with the warehouse manager.
systems: WMS such as Unicommerce, Increff, Vinculum or SAP EWM
automations.data: Mostly business data about goods, suppliers and vehicles, plus driver names and phone numbers at the gate. Photos are linked to the receipt and kept for the client's claim window. Each client sees only its own receipts through role-based access, and driver details are visible only to gate and dock staff.
kpis: GRN summaries sent within the agreed time
outputs: ASN intake and validation for each client format
GRN summary template with photo evidence
Discrepancy case tracker and weekly report

automations.title: E-way bill validity watch with extension and Part B alerts
automations.summary: Compare each active e-way bill's validity with the vehicle's GPS position and ETA, warn the trip owner before expiry, prompt Part B updates when goods change vehicles, and prepare extension details for an authorized user to submit.
automations.problem: Trucks wait at hubs, break down or queue at consignee gates while e-way bills run out, and transshipments need Part B updated before goods move to another vehicle. Operations teams often find out when an officer stops the vehicle, and goods moving on an expired e-way bill can be detained with penalties.
automations.trigger: An e-way bill is linked to a trip, the GPS-based ETA moves past the validity end, the bill enters its extension window, or a vehicle change is recorded at a hub.
steps: Read the active e-way bills for each trip through the client's GSP or ERP integration, with validity end, distance and vehicle number.
Compare remaining validity with the GPS-based ETA and current position, and flag bills that will expire before delivery.
Alert the trip owner when the extension window opens, with the current location, remaining distance and a draft reason, such as transshipment or accident, for the authorized user to confirm.
When a vehicle change is logged at a hub, remind the hub team to update Part B with the new vehicle number before loading.
Prepare the extension details for an authorized user to review and submit through the portal or API, then record the new validity on the trip.
Report bills expired in transit, extensions and late Part B updates by lane, branch and customer.
automations.humanCheckpoint: An authorized user at the transporter reviews and submits every extension and Part B update. The automation never generates, extends or cancels an e-way bill on its own, and any interception or detention by officers is handled by the branch manager.
systems: E-way bill system via GSP or ERP
automations.data: Uses GST document details, vehicle numbers and trip locations. Access is limited to operations and compliance users at the transporter and to the consignor's nominated contacts. API credentials sit in a secrets vault, and logs are retained as agreed with the client's tax advisor.
kpis: Part B updated before vehicle change
outputs: Extension window and Part B alerts

automations.title: Customs document checklist and clearance status updates
automations.summary: Build a document checklist for each shipment from commodity, HS code, Incoterm and destination, chase missing documents from the shipper, and keep importers and exporters updated as filing, assessment, duty payment and out of charge progress.
automations.problem: Clearance stalls on a missing certificate of origin, an invoice that does not match the packing list or a permit nobody asked for. Documentation teams chase shippers by email, Bills of Entry are filed late or amended, and customers call several times a day to ask whether goods are out of charge while port and CFS free time runs down.
automations.trigger: A shipment is booked or pre-alerted, the vessel or flight ETA changes, a document arrives, or the customs broker's filing system records a new status.
steps: Generate a checklist for each shipment from commodity, HS code, Incoterm, origin and destination: commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, certificate of origin, licenses and other agency permits.
Request missing documents from the shipper or consignee by email or WhatsApp, with due dates set from the arrival date and the Bill of Entry filing timeline.

Use an AI model to cross-check the invoice, packing list and bill of lading for mismatched values, quantities, weights, consignee names and HS codes, and flag differences for the documentation executive.
Read filing, query, assessment, duty payment and out-of-charge statuses from the customs broker's system and the ICEGATE messages it receives, and post milestones to the shipment record.
Send the customer approved milestone updates, and alert the team when a query is raised or free time at the port or CFS is running out.
Report clearance time, queries and amendments by port, commodity and customer.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The licensed customs broker reviews every document set, decides classification, valuation and exemption claims, and files and signs declarations on ICEGATE. AI flags mismatches but never changes a declaration, and the importer approves every duty payment.
systems: Freight forwarding software such as CargoWise
automations.data: Commercial documents carry business data and named contacts; personal data is limited to contacts and signatories. Documents are stored with the shipment and accessible to documentation staff and the customer's nominated contacts. Supporting documents are retained for the period customs regulations require, as confirmed with the customs broker.
kpis: Documents complete before vessel or flight arrival
Clearance time from filing to out of charge
outputs: Checklist rules by commodity, mode and destination
Clearance milestone feed and customer updates

automations.title: Proactive delay and SLA breach alerts with customer updates
automations.summary: Watch every shipment and warehouse order against its promised date or SLA, flag delays, stuck consignments, missed cut-offs and free-time risks early, give each exception an owner, and tell the customer before they have to ask.
automations.problem: Tracking data exists in the TMS, carrier portals, GPS dashboards and the WMS, but nobody watches all of it against what was promised. Delays surface when the customer calls, key accounts hear about rollovers or breakdowns late, warehouse orders miss the carrier cut-off unnoticed, and the same lanes, hubs and carriers fail repeatedly without data to show it.
automations.trigger: A milestone is missed or late against plan, the ETA moves past the promised date, a shipment shows no scan or GPS movement beyond the agreed limit, or an SLA timer nears breach.
steps: Pull milestones from the TMS, courier and carrier tracking APIs, GPS platforms, WMS order status and shipping line or airline feeds into one timeline with the promised date and SLA.

Run rules for missed pickups, no-movement, stuck-at-hub, ETA slippage, vessel rollovers, free-time expiry and warehouse orders not packed before the carrier cut-off, tuned per lane, service and client.
Create an exception with an owner, reason code and deadline in the control-tower queue, and alert the owner in Slack.
Send the consignee or shipper an approved WhatsApp, SMS or email update with the revised ETA; for key accounts, the account manager approves the message first.
Escalate exceptions still open near the SLA limit to the branch or operations head.
Report exceptions, causes and SLA performance by lane, hub, carrier and client for the weekly review.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Control-tower executives own every exception, confirm the reason before messages go to key accounts, and decide rerouting, upgrades and any cost or claim commitment. Customers are never promised compensation by an automated message.
systems: Carrier, shipping line and airline tracking APIs
automations.data: Uses shipment details and consignee names, phone numbers and addresses only for delivery updates. Messages follow the consent records and opt-outs held for each contact and never include promotions. Location history is kept for the agreed claim window, and customers see only their own shipments.
kpis: Exceptions flagged before the customer contacts you
outputs: Unified shipment timeline and milestone feed
Exception rules per lane, service and client

automations.title: Tracking-grounded support assistant on WhatsApp and web
automations.summary: Answer where-is-my-shipment, delivery slot, document and stock questions on WhatsApp and web chat from live tracking and WMS data, and hand over to an agent with full context whenever a person is needed.
automations.problem: Support teams spend much of the day reading tracking screens back to customers. Consignees ask about deliveries, importers about clearance and 3PL clients about receipts and orders. After hours nobody answers, and general chatbots that guess instead of checking the data create more calls than they save.
automations.trigger: A consignee, shipper or client sends a message on WhatsApp or web chat, or replies to a tracking notification.
steps: Identify the shipment or order from the AWB, booking, container or order number, and verify the requester through the registered phone number or a one-time code before sharing details.
Retrieve live status from the TMS, tracking APIs or WMS, and answer only from that data and the approved FAQ and service policies.
Handle routine requests such as a delivery slot, an address landmark or a document copy within the rules set for each customer.
Hand over to an agent with the conversation, shipment data and a suggested next step when the request involves a claim, damage, a refund, an address change outside the rules or an unhappy customer.
Log every conversation with intent and outcome, and review a weekly sample of answers for accuracy.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Support agents handle claims, damage reports, refunds, complaints and any change to delivery terms. The assistant states only what the data shows, says so when it does not know, and sends low-confidence answers to an agent.
systems: Helpdesk such as Freshdesk or Zoho Desk
Approved FAQ and service policy documents
automations.data: Shares shipment details only after verifying the requester, and shows masked addresses and phone numbers. Conversations are kept for the agreed support retention period. Model APIs are configured so customer conversations are not used for model training, and access to logs is limited to support leads.
outputs: Assistant connected to tracking and WMS data

automations.title: NDR resolution with consignee re-attempt choices
automations.summary: When a delivery fails, confirm the reason with the consignee, offer a re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact or self-pickup, write the choice back to the courier platform before the next dispatch plan, and flag questionable attempts for review.
automations.problem: Failed deliveries come back with codes such as consignee not available, refused or address incomplete, and some are recorded without a real attempt. Merchants chase consignees by phone, re-attempt instructions arrive after the rider has left, and shipments that could have been delivered become return-to-origin costs for the merchant and the courier.
automations.trigger: The rider app records a failed attempt with an NDR reason code, or a consignee replies to an out-for-delivery message to say they will not be available.
steps: Read the NDR event with reason code, attempt time, rider GPS position and call log from the courier platform.

Send the consignee an approved WhatsApp template where opt-in exists, or a DLT-registered SMS, confirming the attempt and offering a re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact, pickup point or cancellation.
Capture the reply through quick-reply buttons; an AI model classifies free-text replies, and unclear ones go to an NDR agent.
Write the instruction back to the courier platform before the next dispatch planning cut-off, and update the merchant through the portal or API.
Flag attempts where the consignee disputes the reason, the rider's GPS position was far from the address or no call was placed, and send them to the hub supervisor.
Mark shipments for return to origin only after the agreed number of attempts or on the merchant's instruction.
automations.humanCheckpoint: NDR agents handle unclear replies and disputes, hub supervisors review flagged attempts and rider conduct, and the merchant decides returns for COD and high-value shipments. Address changes to another city or pin code need the merchant's approval.
systems: Rider app with GPS and call logs
Masked calling provider such as Exotel or Knowlarity
automations.data: Consignee names, phone numbers and addresses are used only to complete the delivery and are masked from riders and agents where the platform allows. WhatsApp is used only with a valid opt-in, such as a checkout opt-in that names the courier, or from the merchant's own account, and messages carry no promotions. Reply logs are kept for the merchant dispute window and then deleted.
kpis: NDRs resolved by the next attempt
outputs: NDR message templates with consignee choices
Write-back of instructions to the courier platform
NDR and RTO dashboard by hub and merchant

automations.title: Digital POD capture and freight invoice drafting
automations.summary: Capture proof of delivery with photos, stamp or OTP, unloading times and remarks in the driver app or on WhatsApp, match it to the LR, and turn complete PODs into draft freight invoices with detention and other charges for finance to approve.
automations.problem: Physical POD copies travel back with drivers or by courier, sometimes weeks after delivery. Billing waits for them, shippers reject invoices without a POD, detention and unloading charges go unclaimed because nobody recorded the times, and receivables stretch while finance chases paperwork.
automations.trigger: A driver marks a trip delivered in the app, sends a POD photo on WhatsApp, or the consignee confirms receipt with an OTP or e-signature.
steps: Collect POD photos, consignee stamp or signature, OTP confirmation, arrival and unloading times and any shortage or damage remarks through the driver app or WhatsApp.
Use OCR and an AI model to read the LR number, consignee stamp, date and remarks, match them to the trip, and flag missing stamps, unreadable images or noted shortages.
Calculate freight from the contract rate card and add detention, loading, multi-point or toll charges from recorded times and the contract terms.
Create a draft invoice in the accounting system with POD and LR images attached, and route it to the billing executive for review.
Send approved invoices with PODs to the shipper's billing contact or portal, and track acknowledgement and payment due dates.
Report POD collection time, unbilled trips and invoice disputes by customer and branch.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The billing executive reviews every draft invoice, and the finance controller approves detention or other charges outside the contract and any credit note. PODs with shortage or damage remarks go to the claims owner before billing.
systems: GST invoicing in the ERP, with e-invoicing where it applies
automations.data: PODs carry consignee names, signatures and stamps, so images are stored with access limited to billing, operations and the shipper's nominated contacts. Driver phone numbers are used only for trip communication. The client's accountant confirms whether e-invoicing applies to its freight services and how long invoices are kept.
kpis: Trips unbilled after the agreed days
Detention charges billed against detention recorded
outputs: Digital POD capture in the driver app and WhatsApp

automations.title: COD cash and remittance reconciliation
automations.summary: Reconcile cash-on-delivery collections from rider cash, UPI and card payments at the doorstep against delivered AWBs, flag short deposits and mismatches daily, and prepare merchant remittance files and statements for finance to release.
automations.problem: COD money moves through riders, branch cash, bank deposits, UPI collections and payment gateways before it reaches the merchant. Finance reconciles by AWB in spreadsheets, short deposits and duplicate entries surface weeks later, and merchants chase remittances and dispute deductions because statements do not tie back to their orders.
automations.trigger: The daily delivery and collection export closes, a branch records a cash deposit, a bank or payment gateway settlement arrives, or a merchant remittance cycle falls due.
steps: Pull delivered COD AWBs, rider cash collections, branch deposit records, bank statements and UPI or card settlement reports into one daily dataset.
Match collections to AWBs and deposits to collections, and flag short or late deposits by rider and branch, duplicate payments and delivered COD shipments with no collection.
Send branch managers a daily list of open mismatches with rider names and amounts, and track each to resolution.
Build merchant remittance files for each cycle with AWB-level detail and freight and RTO deductions, and record the bank UTR against each remittance once finance releases it.
Send merchants a statement with each remittance and route their disputes to the finance owner.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The finance controller approves every remittance batch before payment. Short deposits and suspected cash misuse are investigated by the branch manager and HR, never acted on by the automation, and disputed merchant deductions are held until a person decides.
systems: Bank statements and payment gateway settlements
automations.data: Financial data about merchants and named riders, so access is limited to finance, branch managers and each merchant's own statements. Bank and gateway connections are read-only, with credentials in a secrets vault. Records follow accounting retention requirements, and rider-level discrepancy data is shared only with the people investigating it.
kpis: Remittances paid on the agreed cycle

automations.title: Trip expense and fuel claims with GPS and fuel card checks
automations.summary: Let drivers submit fuel, toll, loading and repair expenses with receipt photos on WhatsApp, check them against fuel card, FASTag and GPS data, and give the fleet manager a short list of exceptions to approve before the trip is settled.
automations.problem: Drivers carry cash advances and return with a bundle of receipts. Accounts check them by hand against trip sheets, fuel bills do not tie to kilometers driven, toll claims overlap with FASTag deductions, and settlements drag on. Honest drivers wait for their money while questionable claims slip through.
automations.trigger: A driver sends an expense photo or voice note during a trip, a trip is closed in the TMS, or fuel card and FASTag statements arrive.
steps: Collect receipts, odometer photos and voice notes from drivers on WhatsApp during the trip and attach them to the trip record.
Use OCR and an AI model to extract date, amount, vendor, fuel quantity and location from each receipt, and ask the driver for anything missing.
Cross-check fuel against fuel card transactions and expected consumption for the vehicle and route, tolls against FASTag statements, and claimed locations against the GPS track.
Calculate the settlement against the advance and the expense policy, and list exceptions such as duplicate tolls, fuel beyond tolerance or missing receipts.
Send the fleet manager the settlement with exceptions for approval, then post the approved entry to accounts and inform the driver.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The fleet manager approves every settlement and decides on exceptions after hearing the driver. Flags are prompts for a conversation, not findings of misconduct, and any deduction or disciplinary step is decided by the manager and HR.
systems: Fuel card statements such as IndianOil XTRAPOWER
automations.data: Driver names, phone numbers, location tracks and expense records are personal data used only for trip settlement. Access is limited to the fleet manager, accounts and each driver's own records. Receipts and settlements follow accounting retention requirements, and GPS tracks used for checks are kept only for the agreed period.
outputs: Fuel card, FASTag and GPS cross-checks
Settlement approval screen with posting to accounts

automations.title: Client stock statements and activity-based 3PL billing
automations.summary: Send each 3PL client scheduled stock, ageing and near-expiry statements from the WMS, and build monthly invoices from storage, handling and value-added activity under each contract, with exceptions reviewed before finance approves.
automations.problem: Clients ask for stock reports in their own formats, and the warehouse team builds them by hand from WMS exports. Billing for pallet storage, inbound and outbound handling, kitting, relabeling and returns is assembled at month-end from several reports, charges are missed or disputed, and invoices go out late.
automations.trigger: A client's scheduled report time, month-end close, or an ad hoc statement request from a client through the portal.
steps: Pull daily inventory snapshots and inbound, outbound, returns and value-added service logs for each client from the WMS into a warehouse data model.
Send scheduled stock statements with ageing, batch, near-expiry, damaged and quarantined lines to each client's nominated contacts or portal.
Calculate storage by pallet, bin or area per day and handling charges from each contract rate card, including minimum commitments and special rates.
List exceptions such as activities without a rate, unusual volumes or stock held in quarantine beyond the agreed limit, and send them to the account manager.
Create the draft invoice with an activity annexure for the finance controller to approve, then send both to the client.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The account manager reviews exceptions and rate questions, and the finance controller approves every invoice and credit note. Decisions on near-expiry and quarantined stock, such as liquidation, return or destruction, belong to the client and are recorded against their nominated contact.
systems: WMS such as Unicommerce, Increff, Vinculum or SAP EWM
automations.data: Mostly business data about client stock and activity. Each client sees only its own data through role-based access, and rate cards and margins are restricted to account management and finance. Invoice and activity records follow GST and accounting retention requirements.
outputs: Warehouse data model for each client
Billing engine based on contract rate cards

examples: LR booking and trip management systems
systems.role: System of record for bookings, AWBs or LRs, trips, milestones and delivery outcomes. We read through APIs, webhooks or scheduled exports and write back only agreed instructions or status fields, such as re-attempt choices.

Holds item masters, ASNs, receipts, inventory, orders and value-added activity for each client. We read events and snapshots for alerts, statements and billing, and never post inventory adjustments without the warehouse manager.

Hold bookings, house and master bills, documents and customs declarations. Automations read status and documents to build checklists and updates; filing and signing stay with the licensed customs broker.
Provide location, odometer, toll crossings and vehicle and driver records. We use them for ETAs, maintenance and document checks, with access limited to operational purposes.

examples: E-way bill system via GSP or ERP
E-invoice IRP via ERP or GSP
systems.role: Generate and hold statutory documents. Workflows read e-way bill and invoice status and alert people; authorized users generate, extend, cancel and file.

examples: Masked calling such as Exotel or Knowlarity
Helpdesk such as Freshdesk or Zoho Desk
systems.role: Carry bookings, updates, NDR choices and support conversations. Templates, consent records and opt-outs are managed so shipment updates never carry promotions.

examples: Payment gateway and UPI settlement reports
systems.role: Hold invoices, receivables, remittances and expense postings. Automations prepare drafts and reconciliations; finance approves postings and payments.

kpis.name: On-time delivery against promise
kpis.definition: Share of shipments delivered by the date and time promised to the customer or set in the SLA, by lane, service, hub and carrier.
kpis.why: The measure customers judge you on; the breakdown shows whether planning, line haul or the last mile is failing.

kpis.name: First-attempt delivery rate
kpis.definition: Share of shipments out for delivery that are delivered on the first attempt, excluding reschedules the consignee requested in advance.
kpis.why: Every failed attempt costs a trip, delays COD cash and raises the chance of a return to origin.

kpis.name: Return-to-origin rate
kpis.definition: Share of shipments in a period returned to the merchant after failed attempts or refusal, by merchant, pin code and reason.
kpis.why: Returns cost both the merchant and the network; reason-coded data separates fixable causes from genuine refusals.

kpis.name: Exception resolution time
kpis.definition: Median time from an exception being raised, such as a delay, no-movement or failed attempt, to its recorded resolution, by exception type and owner.
kpis.why: Shows whether the control tower acts quickly and where ownership or escalation is weak.

kpis.name: POD-to-invoice time
kpis.definition: Median days from delivery to a complete POD on file, and from POD to invoice sent, by customer and branch.
kpis.why: Billing that waits for paper stretches receivables; the split shows whether POD collection or billing review is the bottleneck.

kpis.name: COD reconciliation lag
kpis.definition: Median days from a COD delivery to the collection being matched to a deposit and included in a merchant remittance, with unreconciled value by aging.
kpis.why: Merchants judge couriers on remittance speed and accuracy, and unmatched cash is a control risk.

kpis.name: Dock-to-stock time
kpis.definition: Median hours from a vehicle reporting at the dock to received goods being available for picking in the WMS, by client.
kpis.why: Clients cannot sell stock still sitting on the dock; delays here lead to stock-outs and disputes.

kpis.name: Quote turnaround time
kpis.definition: Median business hours from a complete rate request to an approved quote being sent, by mode, lane and customer tier.
kpis.why: Shippers often book with the first complete, valid quote; this shows whether pricing capacity or approvals slow you down.

kpis.name: Clearance time
kpis.definition: Median time from Bill of Entry or shipping bill filing to out of charge or let export order, with waiting time attributed to queries and missing documents.
kpis.why: Points at document quality and query handling, which drive demurrage, detention and customer satisfaction.

kpis.name: Document and permit lapses
kpis.definition: Count of vehicles, drivers or riders with an expired license, registration, insurance, PUC, fitness certificate or permit during the period, plus e-way bills expired in transit.
kpis.why: Each lapse is a legal, insurance and service risk; the aim is to see them coming, not to count them afterwards.

phases.title: Discover
phases.description: We map how bookings, trips, receipts, documents, exceptions, PODs and settlements actually flow, sit with the booking desk, control tower, hub, warehouse, fleet and billing teams, and pick the workflows where automation helps most. We baseline KPIs from TMS, WMS, GPS and accounting data and identify GST, customs, messaging and personal data boundaries early.
deliverables: Current-state maps for the selected workflows
Data source inventory covering TMS, WMS, GPS, forwarding software, accounts and portals
Prioritized automation backlog with effort and risk
KPI baseline and measurement plan
clientInputs: Read access or sample exports from the TMS, WMS, GPS platform and accounts
Time with booking, control-tower, hub, warehouse, fleet and billing staff
Customer contracts, SLAs, rate cards and approval matrices

phases.title: Design
phases.description: We design each workflow with its triggers, data fields, decision rules, approval points and failure paths, plus the WhatsApp and SMS templates, driver and rider flows and review screens people will use. We agree which actions stay with authorized users, such as e-way bill extensions and customs filings, and how consent is collected for consignee and driver messages.
deliverables: Workflow designs with human checkpoints and exception paths
Integration plan for TMS, WMS, GPS, GSP, forwarding and messaging systems
WhatsApp, SMS and driver-app message designs
Access, consent and retention design
clientInputs: Rate, claims, remittance and expense rules approved by their owners
Consignee and driver notice and consent wording reviewed by the client's legal or compliance owner
Confirmation from the customs broker and tax advisor of the steps that stay with them

phases.title: Build
phases.description: We build integrations, workflows, review screens and dashboards in a test environment using sample or masked data, with logging, alerts and role-based access from the start. Each workflow is demonstrated to its owners with real scenarios from their lanes, hubs and clients as it takes shape.
deliverables: Working workflows in a test environment
TMS, WMS, GPS, accounting and WhatsApp integrations
Review and approval screens for pricing, billing, fleet and NDR teams
Dashboards built on the agreed KPI definitions
Run logs, alerts and error handling
clientInputs: API credentials or service accounts with least-privilege access
WhatsApp Business account verification, template submissions and DLT template registration
Test data and named testers from each team

phases.title: Validate & launch
phases.description: Owners test each workflow against real situations: failed deliveries with disputed reasons, partial receipts, rollovers, expiring e-way bills, short COD deposits and unreadable PODs. We launch with one branch, hub, client, port or lane first, run alongside the current process for a short period, and train approvers and exception handlers.
deliverables: User acceptance results signed off by owners
Parallel-run comparison with the current process
Training for approvers, agents and exception handlers
Go-live checklist and rollback plan
clientInputs: Named owners to sign off each workflow
A pilot branch, hub, client, port or lane
Communication to drivers, riders, merchants or clients about the change

phases.title: Operate & improve
phases.description: We monitor runs, failures, message delivery and AI accuracy, review KPIs with owners each month, tune rules, thresholds and prompts, and add workflows from the backlog. Changes to rate cards, SLAs, portals or regulations follow the same design, test and approval route as the original build.
deliverables: Monthly KPI and exception review
Sampled AI accuracy checks with prompt and rule updates
Incident log with fixes and preventive actions
Updated backlog and roadmap
clientInputs: Monthly review time with the business owner
Feedback from agents, drivers, riders and clients
Advance notice of new clients, contracts, rate cards or system changes

pilot.title: Exception and NDR pilot for one hub, region or lane
pilot.description: A four to six week pilot that connects tracking events for one hub, region or lane, flags delays and failed deliveries, sends approved consignee updates and NDR choices, and gives the control tower one exception queue. Forwarders can pilot the customs checklist for one port instead, and fleets the document register with e-way bill alerts. We compare results with the baseline and decide together whether to extend.
scope: Milestone feed from the TMS or courier platform and GPS for one hub, region or lane
Delay, no-movement and failed-delivery rules with owners and deadlines
Approved WhatsApp and DLT-registered SMS templates for delay updates and NDR choices
Write-back of re-attempt instructions and an exception queue for the control tower
KPI comparison with the baseline, followed by a go or no-go review

governance: The TMS, WMS, forwarding software and accounts stay the systems of record. Automations write only agreed instructions, drafts or status fields, and never generate e-way bills, file customs declarations or post invoices without a named authorized user.

A written approval matrix names who decides rates, margins, claims, credit notes, remittances, expense deductions, returns and driver or rider eligibility, and every approval is logged against that person.

Consignee, driver and rider data is minimized: masked numbers and addresses where platforms allow, consent and opt-out records, role-based access, retention periods per data type, and breach steps designed around the DPDP Act and Rules.

Customer messages use approved WhatsApp templates and DLT-registered SMS service templates, carry no promotions unless the person agreed to them, and never promise compensation, refunds or delivery times the operations team has not confirmed.
AI output is labeled as a draft or classification with links to its source data, low-confidence cases go to people, and samples are checked for accuracy every month.
Every workflow has run logs, failure alerts, an exception owner and a rollback plan, and credentials sit in a secrets vault with least-privilege, read-only access wherever writing is not needed.

compliance.title: GST e-way bills: validity, Part B and extensions (CGST Rule 138)
compliance.description: Goods worth more than ₹50,000 per consignment generally move with an e-way bill. Validity runs one day per 200 km, or per 20 km for over-dimensional cargo; Part B must be updated before goods change vehicles; and the transporter in charge may extend validity from eight hours before to eight hours after expiry. Since January 2025, the portal rejects bills on documents older than 180 days and extensions beyond 360 days. GSTN revises portal rules by advisory.

compliance.title: Motor Vehicles Act and CMVR documents for vehicles and drivers
compliance.description: When asked, drivers must produce a license of the right class, the registration certificate, insurance and PUC certificate, plus the fitness certificate and permit for transport vehicles. Rule 139 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, amended in 2018, accepts these in electronic form, and MoRTH's procedure recognizes DigiLocker and mParivahan copies. Workflows take expiry dates from the documents and VAHAN or SARATHI records, and the fleet manager decides exceptions.

compliance.title: Customs filing on ICEGATE and Bill of Entry timelines
compliance.description: Bills of Entry and shipping bills are filed on ICEGATE by the importer, exporter or a licensed customs broker, with supporting documents uploaded through e-Sanchit. Under Section 46 of the Customs Act as amended in 2021, a Bill of Entry is generally due before the end of the day preceding arrival; the Board may allow later limits in some cases, and late filing without sufficient cause attracts charges. Automations track checklists and status; the broker files and signs.

compliance.title: Carriage by Road Act, 2007 for common carriers
compliance.description: Businesses that collect, store, forward or deliver goods by road for hire, including booking agents and courier agencies, need a certificate of registration as a common carrier. The consignor executes a goods forwarding note declaring the value and any dangerous or hazardous goods, and the carrier issues a goods receipt; liability follows these documents. Booking flows can capture the declaration and produce the documents, with exceptions reviewed by the booking desk.

compliance.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025
compliance.description: Consignees, merchants' customers, drivers and riders are data principals. The DPDP Rules were notified on 13 November 2025 in phases: consent manager provisions from November 2026 and most duties, including notice, consent, security safeguards, breach intimation and erasure, from May 2027. MeitY has consulted on bringing dates forward, so we design for them now. Merchant and brand contracts name the data fiduciary and the processor. GDPR may apply to EU contacts.

compliance.title: Messaging consent on WhatsApp, SMS and calls
compliance.description: WhatsApp requires an opt-in that names the business, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window and a clear path to a person in automated chats, and since January 2026 Meta bars general-purpose AI assistants, so ours answer only about the client's shipments. SMS and calls follow TRAI's TCCCPR, amended in February 2025 and September 2026: DLT-registered headers and templates, with delivery and NDR updates sent as service messages without promotions.

faqs.question: Do we need to replace our TMS, WMS or forwarding software?
faqs.answer: No. Your TMS or courier platform, WMS, forwarding software and accounts stay the systems of record. We connect through their APIs, webhooks, EDI or scheduled exports and write back only agreed fields, such as re-attempt instructions, exception status or draft invoices. Where a system has no API, we start with exports and agree a path to a sturdier integration.

faqs.question: Will the automation generate or extend e-way bills or file customs declarations?
faqs.answer: No. Workflows read e-way bill and customs status, alert the right people and prepare the details. An authorized user at your company submits e-way bill extensions and Part B updates, and your licensed customs broker classifies, values, files and signs declarations on ICEGATE.

faqs.question: Can we send delivery updates and NDR choices on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the WhatsApp Business Platform via Meta or an approved provider, to consignees who opted in to messages from the sender, for example at a merchant checkout that names the courier, or from the merchant's own WhatsApp account. Messages outside the 24-hour customer service window use templates approved by WhatsApp. Without a WhatsApp opt-in, the same choices go by SMS on DLT-registered service templates. Messages carry no promotions and every opt-out is honored.

faqs.question: How do you protect consignee, driver and rider data?
faqs.answer: We collect only the fields each workflow needs, mask phone numbers and addresses for riders and agents where the platform allows, keep documents encrypted with role-based access, and agree retention periods per data type. Contracts with merchants and clients set out who acts as data fiduciary and who as processor, and notices, consent records and breach response steps are designed around the DPDP Act and Rules.

faqs.question: Will AI decide claims, deductions or driver eligibility?
faqs.answer: No. AI reads documents, classifies replies, drafts quotes and invoices, and answers tracking questions from your data. Pricing leads approve rates, finance approves invoices, remittances and settlements, fleet and HR managers decide driver and rider eligibility and any deduction, and claims owners decide claims. Every approval is logged against a named person.

faqs.question: Does this work with attached market vehicles, not just our own fleet?
faqs.answer: Yes. Document collection and expiry tracking work for attached vehicles and their owners, and POD and expense capture run on WhatsApp, so drivers need no extra app. Where GPS is not fitted, location can come from consent-based phone tracking or FASTag toll crossings where your ULIP access includes them. Vehicle and license checks use VAHAN and SARATHI records with the owner's and driver's consent.

faqs.question: How long before something is live?
faqs.answer: A first pilot usually takes four to six weeks from discovery to a working workflow for one hub, lane, client or port, depending on access to systems and how quickly approval rules and message templates are agreed. Larger workflows such as RFQ-to-quote or the tracking assistant are delivered in stages.

faqs.question: How do you measure whether it worked?
faqs.answer: We baseline the agreed KPIs during Discover, such as first-attempt delivery rate, exception resolution time, POD-to-invoice time or quote turnaround, and review them with you every month after launch. We do not promise fixed improvements in advance; the numbers come from your own data.
